prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1291; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a two-vehicle collision in Conroe, Texas, where the vehicles came together in a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 was operating the first vehicle and Driver 2 the second. A Passenger was also seated in the first vehicle at the time of the crash. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and said the impact pushed them forward and back against the seat. The damage to both vehicles is consistent with the reported direction and force of the collision, and the front-end deformation on the first vehicle matches the contact area on the second. No earlier damage to the first vehicle was found in the inspection or known to the owner. Officers confirmed through the scene and statements from both drivers and the Passenger that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle when it was struck. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the account, though no independent witnesses came forward. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the first vehicle. Officers documented the scene, issued no citations at the time, and forwarded the report for follow-up.
